title: The Tour: idea to production
summary: One small change, from a new issue to production, driven by real events.

steps.title: An idea becomes an issue
steps.narration: Every change starts as a GitHub issue that says what done looks like. This one is typed by a person, right now. It could just as easily have come from a monitoring alert.

args.title: Add a low-stock products endpoint
args.body:
Store staff want to see which products are about to run out.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/products/low-stock?threshold=` returns products with `stock` below the threshold (default 5), lowest stock first
- [ ] A threshold below 0 returns 400 with a problem details body
- [ ] Covered by unit and integration tests

_Opened by the demo console Tour._

steps.title: An AI triager decides who should do it
steps.narration: Within seconds, a triage job scores the issue for risk and difficulty. Low-risk work goes straight to an agent. Anything risky waits for a human.

failOn.subject: issue#{issue}
failOn.description: Triage sent it to a human instead

steps.title: An agent writes the code and the tests
steps.narration: The agent works in a fresh machine in GitHub Actions. It reads the repo rules, writes the change and its tests, and runs the same checks you would run locally.

wait.description: The agent opens a pull request that closes the issue

steps.title: Every check runs on every PR, in parallel
steps.narration: Build, tests, security scans and an AI review all run at once. A preview copy of the app is live for this PR alone. If the AI review finds a problem, the agent fixes it and the checks run again. Nothing merges unless everything is green.

failOn.subject: pr#{pr}
failOn.description: The AI review blocked the PR twice, so it waits for a person

steps.title: The merge queue keeps main working
steps.narration: Before merging, the queue re-tests the PR on top of the latest main, so two good changes cannot break each other, and builds the image that will ship. Then it merges, with no button pressed.

wait.subject: pr#{pr}
wait.description: The merge queue merges the PR into main

steps.title: Merging is deploying
steps.narration: The image CI already built goes to staging, passes smoke tests, then rolls out to production. If the new version is unhealthy, AWS rolls it back on its own.

wait.subject: prod
wait.description: The new version is live in production

steps.title: Production watches itself
steps.narration: Logs, metrics and alarms track every request. When something breaks, an agent investigates and opens an issue, and the loop starts again.
